packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

reader: Claude Opus 5.5, fresh subagent, prompt and images only; repository and search tools available but forbidden; exposures stated in each response
text:
PACKET-17 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING

Exposure statement
- No proposed identification or earlier reading of this leaf reached me from the task context. I did not search, consult editions, or open packet.json.
- Disclosure: while reading, I recognised from general knowledge that the text is Latin liturgical prayer of the kind used at Mass. I did NOT use memory to fill gaps: words not visible are marked [..] or [illegible]. Where a reading is uncertain I flag it with (?). Recognition can still bias uncertain letters, so please weigh the (?) readings accordingly.
- Labels visible in the images: pencil "VI,c Jk 17" (recto top left, image-002) and pencil shelfmarks "Stams, STA, Frg. 69r" (recto, image-004) and "Stams, STA, Frg. 69v" (verso, image-011). Reported as seen.
- Beyond the rules, I only listed the packet directory to get filenames.

Image inventory
- image-001: overview, face labelled 69r. image-002..007: tiles of 69r (002 upper left, 003 upper centre, 004 upper right, 005 lower left, 006 lower centre, 007 lower right).
- image-008: overview, face labelled 69v. image-009..014: tiles of 69v (009 upper left, 010 upper centre, 011 upper right, 012 lower left, 013 lower centre, 014 lower right).
- All images loaded.

1. Layout survey (observations)
- A single parchment leaf (c. 18 x 15 cm visible on the rule), cut down and with its edges folded in on all four sides (turn-ins, with notches cut at the corners), as for a binding wrapper or cover lining. There are holes along the fold lines. A vertical crease runs down the centre.
- One column of text, ruled in plummet/ink (horizontal ruling visible).
- Main script: a large textualis (gothic book hand) in brown-black ink, c. 17 lines visible on 69v.
- Red: two-line initials (P, M on 69r; P, P, A, P, A, E, H, D on 69v), some with pen hair-line flourishes; small red crosses within the text on 69v line 9; red rubric words on 69r ("Collecta", a "lectio ..." rubric, versicle/response marks).
- 69r: the upper half is in the large script. Below "amen·" (line 9) the text changes to a much smaller module (smaller textualis/semi-cursive), with red initials (G, D, a red "V", "R", "V") and red rubrics. The lower half is heavily faded/abraded. The text on the folded-in bottom flap (protected) is clearer.
- 69v: large script throughout, the best preserved face. After "Agnus dei·" (line 10) the rest of that line is ghost-faint (erased or worn), with a small later pen scribble over it.
- Notation, glosses, running titles: none seen.

2. Areas selected / unread
- 69v: all 17 lines transcribed (the line under l.17 is cut and shows only letter tops).
- 69r: the large-script lines 1-9 and the clearer bottom-flap lines transcribed. The middle zone of the smaller script (between "amen·" and the bottom fold) is mostly unread: very faded, only scattered words/rubrics given.
- Suggest UV/multispectral imaging of the lower half of 69r (image-005/006/007, below the "amen" line) and of 69v line 10.

3. Transcription
Conventions: line numbers are counted per face (L1, L2...), and each line gives the tile(s) it was read from. [..] = lost/unread, [illegible] = present but unreadable, (?) = uncertain. Abbreviations: macron/bar shown as ̄ ; "ꝑ"/"ꝓ" = p with bar/flourish (per/pro); "ꝫ"/";" = -bus/-que sign; expansions in ( ).

=== 69v (image-008..014) - best preserved ===

L7 (img-009/010/011): ihm̄ xp̄m filiū tuū qui tecū uiuit et regnat in uni-
L8 (img-012/013/011/014): tate ſp̄c ſci d's· P(red)er omnia ſecula ſeclo͡ꝝ· amen·
L9 (img-012/013/014): P(red)ax [red cross] dn̄i· ſit ſemꝑ uobiſcum [red cross]· E(red)t cū ſpiritu
L10 (img-012/013/014): tuo· A(red)gnus dei· [later pen scribble] [ghost-faint/erased text, illegible, to end of line]
L11 (img-012/013/014): H(red)ec ſacro ſcā cõmixtio coꝛꝑis et ſanguinis dn̄i
L12 (img-012/013/014): nrī ihu xp̄i· fiat mı̄ et omibz ſum̄tibz ſalus mentis
L13 (img-012/013/014): et coꝛꝑis et ad uitā etn̄am ꝓmerenda et capeſſenda
L14 (img-012/013): ꝑparatio ſalutaris amen·
L15 (img-012/013/014): D(red)n̄e ihu xp̄e fili dei uiui· qui [faded][..] [..]tate(?) ꝑr̄is(?)   (small hole/fold in centre)
L16 (img-012/013/014): cooꝑante ſpū ſcō ꝑmoꝛtē tuā m[..]dū(?) uiui[..] caſti·
L17 (img-012/013/014): liba me q̄ſo ꝑhoc ſacro ſcm̄ coꝛꝑ' et ſanguinē tuū
L18 (img-012/013): [cut: only ascenders/macrons visible]

4. Limitations
- Leaf trimmed on all sides and folded in; line beginnings on the left of 69v are partly in the fold (l.1-4 have lost first letters).
- 69r is heavily stained/faded: much of lines 3-7 (centre) and nearly all of the small-script zone L10-L17 are uncertain or unread. The flap lines F1-F5 are better but still worn at the left. The relation of the small-script zone to the large-script block (same campaign or later addition) is not established from these images.
- Face order (which side is first) is taken only from the pencil r/v labels.
- Unverified image reading.
